A_target.statement: The quotient group $\R^2 / \Z^2$ is [[Definition:Homeomorphic|homeomorphic]] to the torus $\Bbb S^1 \times \Bbb S^1$, and the quotient map $\R^2 \to \R^2 / \Z^2$ is a [[Definition:Covering Map|covering map]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a continuous, [[Definition:Open Mapping|open]], [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]] of [[Definition:Topological Group|topological groups]].
Then $G / \map \ker \phi \cong H$ as topological groups.

substitutions.the homomorphism phi: (x, y) -> (e^(2 pi i x), e^(2 pi i y))

derived.the topological isomorphism: the torus as a quotient of the plane

object_map.reformulation: Realize the torus as the image of the exponential homomorphism and identify its kernel.

validity_conditions: phi is open because it restricts to a homeomorphism on small open squares.
Z^2 acts freely and properly discontinuously, which makes the quotient map a covering.
proof_plan:
Let $\map \phi {x, y} = \tuple {e^{2 \pi i x}, e^{2 \pi i y} }$.
$\phi$ is a continuous surjective homomorphism $\struct {\R^2, +} \to \Bbb S^1 \times \Bbb S^1$.

On each open square of side less than $1$, $\phi$ is a homeomorphism onto an open set, so $\phi$ is open.
By the source result, $\R^2 / \Z^2 \cong \Bbb S^1 \times \Bbb S^1$.

Translations by $\Z^2$ act freely and properly discontinuously, so the quotient map is a covering, and $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^1 \times \Bbb S^1} \cong \Z^2$ is its deck group.
{{qed}}
